newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Cargolux ups some Europe to F.East rates on Oct 15.
newsitem.headline: Cargolux ups some Europe to F.East rates on Oct 15.

text.p: Cargolux Airlines International said it will increase ex-Europe rates to selected Far East destinations, but excluding Japan, from October 15.

"We are going to add 20 pfennig a kg to Germany-originating freight from October 15 while the scale of increases elsewhere in Europe will be inferior and differ from country to country." Pierre Wesner, Cargolux' vice-president, Europe/Africa/Middle East, told Reuters.
The rate increases centred on Singapore, Hong Kong, Taipei, Bangkok and Kuala Lumpur.
"We delayed our decision until we had a clear idea on the market outlook and forwarders were prepared for a fortnight's notice on rate adjustments instead of the customary month," he added.
Cargolux's ex-Europe rates to Japan will remain unchanged.

"This does not indicate a slackening in demand for cargo space to Japan but rather reflects the policy of the main carriers on the route. Frankly, why rates are not being raised is a mystery," Wesner said.

There will be no change in rates to North American destinations where there was "currently a good balance between demand and capacity" but the cargo airline will apply a minor increase on ex-Europe rates to Mexico City.

In a comment on current market conditions, he said there is a strong demand push from Germany and to a lesser extent, from Spain and Italy. Activity in France, the Benelux, the UK and Scandinavia for Cargolux was not as buoyant.
Cargolux would have preferred a more coherent policy on rates increases but had been obliged to follow the prevailing trend of piecemeal adjustments.

"Having no domestic market to speak of, we have quite naturally taken a European view of business. Over the past eight years, we have practised the notion of European freight rates and while other main cargo carriers have said, "Yes, we support this approach", they have done little to bring it about. Indeed, their policy is to perpetuate discrepancies in rates from country to country by keeping rates high in their home markets while dumping in other European countries," he said.

Wesner added: "When your whole business concept is centred on partnership agreements with major forwarders on a European scale, it becomes a very complicated task to adjust rates from country to country which is what the present system demands."
Cargolux operates a fleet of three Boeing 747-400Fs and three Boeing 747-200Fs as well as an additional 747-200F on a wetlease from Atlas Air.
